objective: Proof: on Young-diagram shapes the box-betweenness base is the cut system (d = 2 L1); adding an outer corner that starts a new line needs exactly one three-place knot, B(opposite corner, neighbour, new), and filling a corner needs exactly three, which can sit in the unit square (where they are unique); totals are order-independent.
status: Proved 2026-11-17 (refereed R1: G1 to G4 confirmed; G5 withdrawn, Block): box betweenness on Young diagrams is the cut system (d = 2 L1); a new line needs exactly one knot, B(opposite corner, neighbour, new), unique; a filled cell exactly three, never two (unique within the unit square: computed in 4 x 4 and 5 x 5, not proved); totals order-independent. Withdrawn: 'the states name every placement' (equal states can have different placements; the states name only the new-line pair).
title: Growing the grid: one knot for a new line, three for a filled cell
